Cluster-randomized trials (2-1-1)

Source: vignettes/articles/model-cluster.qmd

The treatment is assigned to whole clusters (schools, clinics); the mediator and outcome are measured on individuals. Part of the Models collection.

Structure cluster-level X to individual M to individual Y (a “2-1-1” design)
Class returned ClusterMediationData
Indirect effect \(a \, b_{\text{between}}\), split into an own-mediator and a spillover part
Routes fit_mediation(engine = "lmer", cluster = ), or extract_mediation() on a pair of lmer fits
Needs lme4; pbkrtest for se_type = "kr" 
library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
has_lme4 <- requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)
has_pbkr <- requireNamespace("pbkrtest", quietly = TRUE)

Fit it

The data below are simulated: 40 schools of 10 students, treatment assigned by school. The formulas hold fixed effects only; the engine adds the random cluster intercept and the cluster-mean and within-cluster terms of the mediator.

set.seed(2026)
J <- 40
n <- 10
cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n)
x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J))
v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)
u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)
cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl])
cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n)
mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school)
cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n)
x <- fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat, treatment = "X",
                   mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school")
class(x)[1]
[1] "medfit::ClusterMediationData"
paths(x)
         a   b_within  b_between    c_prime
0.27198520 0.37955931 0.76969028 0.07722813

The path b_between is the effect of a cluster’s mean mediator on the outcome, b_within the effect of an individual’s deviation from the cluster mean. The indirect effect uses the between-cluster path, because the treatment moves whole clusters.

Read it 

tidy(x, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 5 × 5
  term      estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie         0.209     0.127  -0.0397      0.458
2 nde         0.0772    0.227  -0.368       0.522
3 te          0.287     0.241  -0.186       0.760
4 own         0.103     0.0543 -0.00323     0.210
5 spillover   0.106     0.0886 -0.0675      0.280
decompose(x)
      own spillover       nie
0.1032345 0.1061099 0.2093444
attr(,"label")
[1] "cluster-average, large-cluster approximation"

decompose() splits the indirect effect: own is the part acting through a student’s own mediator, spillover the part acting through the rest of the cluster. The split is a large-cluster approximation (the label on the result says so).

Few clusters

With fewer than 25 clusters and model-based standard errors, medfit warns that the intervals can be too small. Two remedies:

few <- cdat[cdat$school %in% levels(cdat$school)[1:12], ]
few$school <- droplevels(few$school)
fit_few <- function(se) {
  suppressWarnings(fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = few, treatment = "X",
                                 mediator = "M", engine = "lmer",
                                 cluster = "school", se_type = se))
}
rbind(model = confint(fit_few("model"))["b_between", ],
      kr = confint(fit_few("kr"))["b_between", ])
           2.5 %   97.5 %
model -0.7218072 1.236564
kr    -0.8727810 1.387538
  • se_type = "kr" gives Kenward-Roger t intervals for the paths. They are wider, as they should be with 12 clusters (the example above shows the b_between interval widening).
  • A cluster bootstrap resamples whole clusters, which is the safer interval for the product effects:
nie_of <- function(dd) {
  unname(nie(fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = dd, treatment = "X",
                           mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school")))
}
bootstrap_mediation(nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat,
                    cluster = "school", n_boot = 200, seed = 123)
Warning in .bootstrap_nonparametric_cluster(data, statistic_fn, n_boot, : 3
bootstrap samples failed and were excluded (3 of them singular or
non-convergent refits)
BootstrapResult object
======================

Method:   nonparametric
Estimate:   0.2093
N bootstrap samples: 197

95% Confidence Interval:
  Lower:  -0.0038
  Upper:   0.5241

A warning, when it appears, counts the draws dropped as singular or non-convergent refits; the interval uses the rest.

Already have lmer fits?

extract_mediation() takes the pair. The outcome model must carry the mediator’s cluster mean and its within-cluster deviation as two terms, and both models need the same rows and the random intercept for the cluster:

cdat$M_cm <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school)
cdat$M_cwc <- cdat$M - cdat$M_cm
fm <- lme4::lmer(M ~ X + (1 | school), cdat)
fy <- lme4::lmer(Y ~ X + M_cwc + M_cm + (1 | school), cdat)
x2 <- extract_mediation(fm, model_y = fy, treatment = "X", mediator = "M")
c(from_lmer_pair = unname(nie(x2)), from_engine = unname(nie(x)))
from_lmer_pair    from_engine
     0.2093444      0.2093444

Limits

  • The treatment must be constant within a cluster. If it varies, fit_mediation() stops with “Treatment X varies within clusters; 1-1-1 designs are not supported yet”.
  • Gaussian linear mixed models only; no glmer. The default is a random intercept. A random slope on the within-cluster mediator term is accepted (engine_args = list(random_y = ~ M)); a slope on the treatment, the cluster mean or the raw mediator is not (for the treatment: “A random slope on the treatment (X) is not supported: it is constant within clusters”).
  • An outcome model without the cluster-mean term fails with a message that names the term to add (for example M_cwc + M_cm).
  • The own and spillover split is a large-cluster approximation, and the interval evidence for the cluster bootstrap is thin; see Methods and Formulas.
